source.text: Ὁ πρεσβύτερος Γαΐῳ τῷ ἀγαπητῷ, ὃν ἐγὼ ἀγαπῶ ἐν ἀληθείᾳ.

records.literal_gloss: The elder to Gaius the beloved, whom I love in truth.

en.L: The elder, to Gaius the beloved, whom I love in truth.
en.B: The elder, to my dear friend Gaius, whom I love in truth.
en.R: From the elder, to my dear friend Gaius. I truly love you, as one who shares the truth with me.

es.L: El anciano, al amado Gayo, a quien yo amo en [la] verdad.
es.B: El anciano, a mi querido amigo Gayo, a quien amo en la verdad.
es.R: Esta carta es del anciano, para mi querido amigo Gayo. Te amo de verdad, como a alguien que comparte conmigo la verdad.

fr.L: L’ancien, à Gaïus le bien-aimé, que j’aime en vérité.
fr.B: L’ancien, à mon cher ami Gaïus, que j’aime dans la vérité.
fr.R: De la part de l’ancien, à mon cher ami Gaïus. Je t’aime vraiment, toi qui partages la vérité avec moi.

sw.L: Mzee, kwa Gayo aliye mpendwa, ninayempenda mimi katika kweli.
sw.B: Mzee, kwa rafiki yangu mpendwa Gayo, ninayempenda katika kweli.
sw.R: Barua hii inatoka kwa mzee, kwa rafiki yangu mpendwa Gayo. Nakupenda kweli, kama mtu anayeshiriki kweli pamoja nami.

ko.L: 장로가, 사랑하는 가이오에게 [편지합니다]. 나는 그를 진리 안에서 사랑합니다.
ko.B: 장로인 내가, 사랑하는 친구 가이오에게 이 편지를 씁니다. 나는 당신을 진리 안에서 사랑합니다.
ko.R: 이 편지는 장로인 내가 사랑하는 친구 가이오에게 보냅니다. 나는 진리를 함께 나누는 사람으로서 당신을 진심으로 사랑합니다.

vi.L: Trưởng lão gửi đến Gai-út yêu dấu, là người tôi yêu thương trong chân lý.
vi.B: Trưởng lão gửi đến anh Gai-út yêu dấu, người mà tôi yêu thương trong chân lý.
vi.R: Thư này của trưởng lão, gửi anh Gai-út thân mến. Tôi thật lòng yêu thương anh, là người cùng tôi sống trong chân lý.

pt.L: O Presbítero, ao amado Gaio, a quem eu amo em verdade.
pt.B: O Presbítero, ao meu querido amigo Gaio, a quem amo em verdade.
pt.R: Do Presbítero, para o meu querido amigo Gaio. Eu amo você de verdade, como alguém que compartilha comigo a verdade.

am.L: ሽማግሌው፣ እኔ በእውነት ለምወደው ለተወደደው ለጋይዮስ።
am.B: ሽማግሌው፣ እኔ በእውነት ለምወደው ለውድ ወዳጄ ለጋይዮስ።
am.R: ይህ ደብዳቤ ከሽማግሌው ነው፤ ለውድ ወዳጄ ለጋይዮስ። እውነትን ከእኔ ጋር የምትካፈል ሰው እንደ መሆንህ በእውነት እወድሃለሁ።

decisions.choice: the elder: a title by which the readers knew the writer
alternatives: an old man, speaking of his age only
decisions.reason: πρεσβύτερος means an older man, and it was the usual word for a leader of a church (Acts 14:23; 20:17; 1 Peter 5:1). With the article and no name it is a title: "the elder", someone the readers knew well and whose word carried weight. 2 John 1 opens the same way. The letter does not name him. From the second century, church tradition has identified him with the apostle John, the writer of John's Gospel and 1 John; some ancient writers also speak of a "John the elder" distinct from the apostle. The letter itself does not settle it.

decisions.choice: Gaius: a believer known to the elder, otherwise unknown to us
decisions.reason: Gaius was one of the commonest Roman first names. The New Testament mentions a Gaius of Macedonia (Acts 19:29), a Gaius of Derbe (Acts 20:4) and a Gaius at Corinth who hosted Paul and the church (Romans 16:23; 1 Corinthians 1:14). Nothing in this letter links this Gaius with any of them. What the letter shows is that he was a believer in a church the elder was concerned with, known for receiving traveling believers into his home (verses 5-8).

decisions.choice: the opening of a letter: writer, then recipient
decisions.reason: Greek letters began "A to B", usually followed by a greeting. This one has no greeting word; the prayer of verse 2 takes its place. The letter is short enough to fit on a single sheet of papyrus, the kind of personal note many letters of the time were.

decisions.choice: love in truth: love that is sincere and grounded in the truth they share
decisions.reason: ἐν ἀληθείᾳ without the article can mean "truly, sincerely". But this short letter uses "truth" six times for the truth of the gospel, which believers hold and live by (verses 3, 4, 8, 12), and 2 John 1-2 puts the two together: the elder loves "in truth", and so do all who know the truth, "because of the truth". Both senses are likely meant here. The emphatic ἐγὼ ("I myself") makes it personal.

decisions.choice: the beloved (Literal); my dear friend (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: ἀγαπητός is the word 1 John uses to address its readers, rendered "Beloved" at Literal and "Dear friends" at Balanced and Readable. "Beloved" is now rare outside church language. "My" is supplied because the elder is speaking of his own affection ("whom I love").

decisions.choice: I truly love you, as one who shares the truth with me
decisions.reason: Readable says both things meaning decision m4 finds in "in truth": the love is real, and it rests on the truth both men hold. It also adds "From" and turns the relative clause into a sentence spoken to Gaius, as letters read today.

decisions.choice: el anciano; amado (L), querido amigo (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 2 John: "anciano" is the word for the elders of the church, used here as a title the readers knew (m1). Literal keeps "amado" (loved one); Balanced and Readable say "querido amigo", as the English says "my dear friend". The same in verses 2, 5 and 11.

decisions.choice: en [la] verdad (L); en la verdad (B)
decisions.reason: As in 2 John 1: without the article, "en verdad" would read only as "truly"; with it, the love is grounded in the truth they share (m4). Readable says "de verdad" and adds the shared truth, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: l’ancien, lowercase (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: As in 2 John: a title the readers knew (m1), written like "les anciens" of the churches, so that it reads as a description, not a name.

decisions.choice: le bien-aimé, Bien-aimé (L); mon cher ami, Cher ami (B, R) (verses 1, 2, 5, 11)
decisions.reason: As the English: "bien-aimé" as an address is church language; "cher ami" is how a French letter addresses a friend.

decisions.choice: mzee; mpendwa (L), rafiki yangu mpendwa (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 2 John: "mzee" is the word for a church elder and a title of respect, fitting a title the readers knew (m1). Literal keeps "mpendwa" (one who is loved); Balanced and Readable say "rafiki yangu mpendwa", as the English says "my dear friend". "Mpenzi" today often means a sweetheart. The same in verses 2, 5 and 11.

decisions.choice: the letter in 합쇼체 at every level, with "당신" for Gaius, the one reader (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: The letter is to one man, a dear friend. As in the Korean of Romans and James for a singular "you", "당신" keeps the letter's 합쇼체; "그대" is warmer but literary, and "형제님", the usual church address, would add a word the Greek does not have. A native reviewer may prefer one of them. Literal keeps the Greek's third person in the opening ("그를"), as the letter heading does.

decisions.choice: "가이오"; "사랑하는 가이오" (L); "사랑하는 친구 가이오" (B, R)
decisions.reason: "가이오" is the established Protestant form of the name. "The beloved" is one dear friend; Balanced and Readable add "친구", as the English does, and "사랑하는 친구여" is the address through the letter (1:2, 5, 11).

decisions.choice: "anh" for Gaius and "tôi" for the elder; "Gai-út", "Đi-ô-trép" (1:9), "Đê-mê-triu" (1:12)
decisions.reason: Gaius is a believer the elder loves and counts among his children (1:4), but he is a grown man with a household that receives travellers, so Vietnamese gives him the warm, respectful "anh", as the Vietnamese Colossians does for Archippus (4:17); the names are in their Protestant forms.

decisions.choice: "yêu dấu" (L, B), "thân mến" (R) for "the beloved"; "Hỡi anh yêu dấu" (L), "Anh yêu dấu" (B), "Anh thân mến" (R) for the address in 1:2, 1:5, 1:11
decisions.reason: "Người yêu" means a sweetheart in Vietnamese, so the singular address is made with "anh"; Readable uses the warm opening of a Vietnamese letter, as for the plural in 1 John.

decisions.choice: o Presbítero, capitalized; Gaio
decisions.reason: As in 2 John 1: the writer's title, by which the readers knew him (meaning decision m1), so it takes a capital at every level. "Gaio" is the Portuguese form of the Roman name, as in Romans 16:23. The elder writes to one man and calls him "você" throughout, as style section 4 has it between people.

decisions.choice: amado (L); meu querido amigo (B, R)
decisions.reason: The same word the first letter uses for its readers, "Amados" (L) and "Meus queridos" (B, R). To one man Balanced and Readable say "meu querido amigo" here and "Querido amigo" as an address in verses 2, 5 and 11, as the English says "Dear friend"; "em verdade" rather than "na verdade", which would mean "actually", as in 2 John 1.

decisions.choice: ሽማግሌው (the elder), as in 2 John 1; ጋይዮስ (Gaius), addressed as አንተ (singular) through the letter
decisions.reason: "ሽማግሌው", with the definite suffix, is the title by which the readers knew the writer (meaning decision m1), the word for the church office of elder in the Amharic of Paul's letters. The letter is written to one man, so every "you" is the familiar singular, as a friend writes to a friend.

decisions.choice: ለተወደደው (to the beloved, L); ለውድ ወዳጄ (to my dear friend, B, R); የተወደድክ ሆይ (L), ወዳጄ ሆይ (B), ውድ ወዳጄ (R) as the address in 2, 5 and 11
decisions.reason: As in 1 John (2:7), now in the singular: Literal keeps the Greek participle, and Balanced and Readable use "ወዳጅ", a friend who is loved, from the root of "መውደድ".

source.text: Ἀγαπητέ, περὶ πάντων εὔχομαί σε εὐοδοῦσθαι καὶ ὑγιαίνειν, καθὼς εὐοδοῦταί σου ἡ ψυχή.

records.literal_gloss: Beloved, concerning all things I pray you to go well and to be healthy, just as goes well your soul.

en.L: Beloved, in all respects I pray that it goes well with you and that you are in good health, just as it goes well with your soul.
en.B: Dear friend, my prayer is that you are doing well in every way and are in good health, just as your soul is doing well.
en.R: Dear friend, I pray that everything is going well for you and that you are healthy in body, just as you are doing well in your life with God.

es.L: Amado, en todo pido en oración que te vaya bien y que tengas buena salud, así como le va bien a tu alma.
es.B: Querido amigo, mi oración es que te vaya bien en todo y que tengas buena salud, así como a tu alma le va bien.
es.R: Querido amigo, pido a Dios que todo te vaya bien y que tengas salud en el cuerpo, así como te va bien en tu vida con Dios.

fr.L: Bien-aimé, en toutes choses je prie pour que tout aille bien pour toi et que tu sois en bonne santé, comme tout va bien pour ton âme.
fr.B: Cher ami, je prie pour que tout aille bien pour toi à tous égards et que tu sois en bonne santé, de même que ton âme se porte bien.
fr.R: Cher ami, je prie pour que tout se passe bien pour toi et que ton corps soit en bonne santé, de même que ta vie avec Dieu va bien.

sw.L: Mpendwa, katika mambo yote naomba uendelee vyema na uwe na afya, kama vile nafsi yako inavyoendelea vyema.

ko.L: 사랑하는 이여, 나는 당신의 영혼이 잘되는 것처럼 당신이 모든 일에 잘되고 건강하기를 기도합니다.
ko.B: 사랑하는 친구여, 당신의 영혼이 잘되고 있는 것처럼 당신이 모든 일에 잘되고 건강하기를 기도합니다.
