vi.L: Hỡi anh yêu dấu, tôi cầu nguyện cho anh được thịnh vượng trong mọi sự và được khỏe mạnh, như linh hồn anh được thịnh vượng.
vi.B: Anh yêu dấu, tôi cầu nguyện cho anh được mọi sự tốt đẹp và được mạnh khỏe, cũng như linh hồn anh đang được tốt đẹp.
vi.R: Anh thân mến, tôi cầu nguyện cho anh được mọi việc tốt đẹp và thân thể được khỏe mạnh, cũng như đời sống của anh với Đức Chúa Trời đang tốt đẹp.

pt.L: Amado, em todas as coisas oro para que tudo vá bem com você e que você tenha saúde, assim como vai bem a sua alma.
pt.B: Querido amigo, a minha oração é que você esteja bem em todos os sentidos e tenha boa saúde, assim como a sua alma vai bem.
pt.R: Querido amigo, eu oro para que tudo esteja indo bem para você e que o seu corpo tenha saúde, assim como vai bem a sua vida com Deus.

am.L: የተወደድክ ሆይ፣ ነፍስህ መልካም እንደ ሆነች፣ በሁሉ ነገር መልካም እንዲሆንልህና ጤናማ እንድትሆን እጸልያለሁ።
am.B: ወዳጄ ሆይ፣ ነፍስህ መልካም እንደ ሆነች ሁሉ፣ በሁሉም ነገር መልካም እንዲሆንልህና ጤናማ እንድትሆን እጸልያለሁ።
am.R: ውድ ወዳጄ፣ ከእግዚአብሔር ጋር ባለህ ሕይወት መልካም እንደ ሆነልህ፣ ሁሉ ነገር መልካም እንዲሆንልህና በሰውነትህም ጤናማ እንድትሆን እጸልያለሁ።

decisions.choice: a prayer for the reader's health: the usual opening of a letter
decisions.reason: Greek letters of the time commonly opened with a wish or prayer that the reader was well and in good health, often with the words "before all things" or "in all things". The elder uses that familiar form and fills it with Christian meaning: he prays to God for his friend. It is an expression of goodwill, as "I hope you are well" is.

decisions.choice: a prayer for a friend, not a promise of wealth or health
alternatives: a promise that believers will prosper materially
decisions.reason: The verse tells what the elder asks for Gaius. It is not a promise to believers that God will make them rich or healthy, and it does not say that bodily well-being follows from spiritual well-being. εὐοδόομαι does not refer to money: it first meant to have a good journey, and then simply for things to go well (in Romans 1:10 it is used of Paul's hope that his way to Rome will be opened). Here it is the ordinary word for being well. The New Testament speaks elsewhere of faithful believers who were sick (Philippians 2:26-27; 2 Timothy 4:20) or poor (2 Corinthians 8:2).

decisions.choice: in all respects
decisions.reason: περὶ πάντων goes with the prayer: may it go well with you in everything. It can also be taken as "above all", as the same words sometimes are in letter openings; the sense is then that this is the first thing the elder prays. Either way the prayer is a full and warm one.

decisions.choice: soul: Gaius's inner life, his life toward God
decisions.reason: ψυχή is the self, the inner person. Here it is set beside bodily health, so it means Gaius's spiritual life, which visitors had already reported to be strong (verse 3). It does not set soul against body as two parts of a person, one more worthy than the other; the elder prays for both.

decisions.choice: it goes well (Literal); doing well (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: "Prosper" now suggests wealth, which the Greek word does not mean here (meaning decision m2). "Doing well" keeps the ordinary sense of a letter's greeting.

decisions.choice: healthy in body; your life with God
decisions.reason: Readable makes the contrast plain: bodily health beside the health of the soul, Gaius's life toward God (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: que te vaya bien; le va bien a tu alma
decisions.reason: "Prosperar" now suggests getting rich, and the meaning decision (m2) says this is a friend's prayer, not a promise of wealth. "Irle bien a alguien" is the everyday Spanish for things going well, and it can be said of the soul as well as of daily life.

decisions.choice: que tout aille bien, se porte bien
decisions.reason: As the English: "prospérer" suggests wealth, which the word does not mean here (m2).

decisions.choice: kuendelea vyema, kwenda vizuri; nafsi
decisions.reason: "Kufanikiwa" today often suggests getting rich, and the meaning decision (m2) says this is a friend's prayer, not a promise of wealth; "kuendelea vyema" is simply doing well. "Nafsi" is the inner self, Gaius's life toward God (m4); "roho" could be taken as the Holy Spirit or a ghost.

decisions.choice: "사랑하는 이여" (L); "사랑하는 친구여" (B, R) for the singular "beloved", through the letter; "영혼" (L, B)
decisions.reason: The singular address keeps the letter's formal "-여" with the plain word for a beloved person at Literal and "친구" at Balanced and Readable. "Soul" is Gaius's inner life toward God (meaning decision), which Readable says. The meaning decision adds that this is a prayer for a friend, not a promise of wealth or health, so Korean keeps "기도합니다".

decisions.choice: "được thịnh vượng" (L) for "go well"
decisions.reason: The verb is the usual wish of a letter that things go well (m1), not a promise of wealth (m2). "Thịnh vượng" can be heard as riches, so only Literal keeps it, for the same word in both halves; Balanced and Readable say "tốt đẹp".

decisions.choice: vá bem, vai bem (L); esteja bem, vai bem (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Prosperar" suggests wealth in Portuguese as "prosper" does in English, which the Greek word does not mean here (meaning decision m2); "ir bem" keeps the ordinary wish of a letter's opening.

decisions.choice: መልካም እንዲሆንልህ (that it may go well with you); ነፍስህ (your soul, L, B), ከእግዚአብሔር ጋር ባለህ ሕይወት (in your life with God, R)
decisions.reason: The prayer is the usual wish for a friend's health at the head of a letter (meaning decisions m1, m2), so it is said with the plain "መልካም እንዲሆንልህ"; "እንዲሳካልህ" would sound like a promise of success. "ነፍስ" is Gaius's inner life toward God (m4); Readable says so, as the English Readable does.

source.text: ἐχάρην γὰρ λίαν ἐρχομένων ἀδελφῶν καὶ μαρτυρούντων σου τῇ ἀληθείᾳ, καθὼς σὺ ἐν ἀληθείᾳ περιπατεῖς.

records.literal_gloss: I rejoiced for greatly [as] coming brothers and testifying of you to the truth, just as you in truth walk.

en.L: For I rejoiced greatly when {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} were coming and testifying to your truth, just as you walk in truth.
en.B: It made me very glad when {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} arrived and testified to your faithfulness to the truth, how you are walking in the truth.
en.R: I was very happy when some believers came here and told me how faithful you are to the truth. They said that you are living by the truth.

es.L: Porque me alegré mucho cuando venían hermanos y daban testimonio de tu verdad, así como tú andas en [la] verdad.
es.B: Me alegró mucho que llegaran hermanos y dieran testimonio de tu fidelidad a la verdad: contaron que andas en la verdad.
es.R: Me puse muy contento cuando llegaron aquí algunos creyentes y me contaron lo fiel que eres a la verdad. Dijeron que vives según la verdad.

fr.L: Car je me suis beaucoup réjoui quand des {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} venaient et rendaient témoignage à ta vérité, comme toi, tu marches dans la vérité.
fr.B: J’ai été très heureux quand des {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} sont arrivés et ont rendu témoignage de ta fidélité à la vérité : ils ont dit comment tu marches dans la vérité.
fr.R: J’ai été très content quand des croyants sont venus ici et m’ont dit combien tu es fidèle à la vérité. Ils ont dit que tu vis selon la vérité.

sw.L: Kwa maana nilifurahi mno ndugu walipokuwa wakija na kushuhudia juu ya kweli yako, kama vile wewe unavyotembea katika kweli.
sw.B: Nilifurahi sana ndugu walipofika na kushuhudia uaminifu wako kwa kweli, jinsi unavyoishi katika kweli.
sw.R: Nilifurahi sana waamini fulani walipofika hapa wakaniambia jinsi ulivyo mwaminifu kwa kweli. Walisema kwamba unaishi kwa kufuata kweli.

ko.L: {{gender:형제자매|형제}}들이 와서 당신의 진리에 대해 증언하였을 때, 곧 당신이 진리 안에서 걷고 있다는 것을 [증언하였을 때], 나는 매우 기뻤습니다.
ko.B: {{gender:형제자매|형제}}들이 와서 당신이 진리에 신실하다는 것, 곧 당신이 진리 안에서 살고 있다는 것을 증언했을 때, 나는 매우 기뻤습니다.
ko.R: 몇몇 믿음의 식구들이 이곳에 와서 당신이 진리에 얼마나 신실한지 말해 주었을 때, 나는 매우 기뻤습니다. 그들은 당신이 진리대로 살고 있다고 말했습니다.

vi.L: Vì tôi đã rất vui mừng khi có {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}} đến và làm chứng về chân lý của anh, như anh đang bước đi trong chân lý.
vi.B: Tôi đã rất vui mừng khi có {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}} đến đây và làm chứng về lòng trung tín của anh đối với chân lý, rằng anh đang bước đi trong chân lý.
vi.R: Tôi rất vui khi có mấy tín hữu đến đây và kể cho tôi biết anh trung tín với chân lý thế nào. Họ nói rằng anh đang sống theo chân lý.

pt.L: Pois me alegrei muito quando vieram {{gender:irmãos e irmãs|irmãos}} e testemunharam da sua verdade, assim como você anda em verdade.
pt.B: Fiquei muito contente quando chegaram {{gender:irmãos e irmãs|irmãos}} e deram testemunho da sua fidelidade à verdade, de como você anda na verdade.
pt.R: Fiquei muito feliz quando chegaram aqui {{gender:alguns irmãos e irmãs na fé|alguns irmãos na fé}} e me contaram como você é fiel à verdade. Eles disseram que você vive de acordo com a verdade.

am.L: {{gender:ወንድሞችና እኅቶች|ወንድሞች}} መጥተው ስለ እውነትህ ሲመሰክሩ እጅግ ደስ ብሎኛልና፤ አንተ በእውነት እንደምትመላለስ።
am.B: {{gender:ወንድሞችና እኅቶች|ወንድሞች}} መጥተው ለእውነት ስላለህ ታማኝነት፣ በእውነትም እንዴት እንደምትመላለስ ሲመሰክሩ እጅግ ደስ አለኝ።
am.R: አንዳንድ አማኞች ወደዚህ መጥተው ለእውነት ምን ያህል ታማኝ እንደ ሆንህ ሲነግሩኝ በጣም ደስ አለኝ። በእውነት እንደምትኖር ነገሩኝ።

decisions.choice: the brothers came and testified, perhaps more than once
decisions.reason: The two participles are present tense, which can picture visitors arriving and reporting on more than one occasion. They can also simply describe one visit. These are traveling believers like those of verses 5-8, who had stayed with Gaius and then told the elder's church about him (verse 6).

decisions.choice: your truth: your faithfulness to the truth
decisions.reason: "Your truth" is the truth as Gaius holds it and lives it: his loyalty to the gospel shown in how he lives. The next clause explains it.

decisions.choice: just as you walk in truth: what the visitors reported
alternatives: as indeed you do walk in the truth
decisions.reason: The clause can give the content of their report (they told how you walk in the truth), or it can be the elder's own confirmation (as indeed you do). The meaning is much the same.

decisions.choice: walk: live, conduct one's life
decisions.reason: περιπατέω is used for a way of life, as in 1 John 1:6-7 and 2:6, and 2 John 4: to walk in the truth is to live by it.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The visitors were fellow believers; the word does not tell us whether they were men or women, and in the plural it covers both. Readable says "believers", which needs no setting.

decisions.choice: your faithfulness to the truth
decisions.reason: Balanced says what "your truth" means (meaning decision m2); Literal keeps the bare phrase.

decisions.choice: told me; living by the truth
decisions.reason: Readable uses everyday words for "testify" and explains the idiom "walk". "Here" and "me" are supplied: the visitors came to the elder.

decisions.choice: hermanos, no setting
decisions.reason: As in 1 John and the other letters, Spanish "hermanos" already covers brothers and sisters, so there is no gender span in this letter.

decisions.choice: passé composé for past events at every level, imperfect for what was repeated (for the whole letter)
alternatives: passé simple at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: A letter speaks to its reader, so French uses the passé composé, as in Colossians. Literal uses the imperfect "venaient et rendaient" for the present participles, which may mean repeated visits (m1).

decisions.choice: des {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} (L, B); des croyants (R) (verses 3, 5, 10)
decisions.reason: As the English: the plural covers men and women; Readable says "croyants", which needs no setting.

decisions.choice: ndugu, no gender span
alternatives: ndugu wa kiume na wa kike
decisions.reason: "Ndugu" already means brothers and sisters, so Swahili needs no gender span in this letter, as in 1 and 2 John.

decisions.choice: "{{gender:형제자매|형제}}들" (L, B) for the travelling believers; "믿음의 식구들" (R) (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: They are fellow believers; Korean uses the span settled for believers as brothers, and Readable says "believers", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}} (L, B); "tín hữu" (R) for the brothers, here and in 1:5 and 1:10
decisions.reason: The brothers are fellow believers, men and women, so Vietnamese uses the gender span; Readable says "believers", as the English Readable does, and "tín hữu" is already inclusive, as in the Vietnamese Colossians (4:15).

decisions.choice: {{gender:alguns irmãos e irmãs na fé|alguns irmãos na fé}}
decisions.reason: The English Readable says "some believers", which needs no setting. Portuguese "crentes" means Protestants in Brazil, so Readable says "irmãos na fé", as 1 John does at Readable, and so needs the gender setting; the same in verses 5 and 10.

decisions.choice: {{gender:ወንድሞችና እኅቶች|ወንድሞች}} (brothers and sisters, or brothers), and the forms with a case ending in verses 5 and 10, with the ending inside each option; አማኞች (believers, R)
decisions.reason: The travellers are fellow believers, men and women, and Amharic can name both, as in 1 John 3:13. Readable says "believers", as the English Readable does, and needs no span.

source.text: μειζοτέραν τούτων οὐκ ἔχω χαράν, ἵνα ἀκούω τὰ ἐμὰ τέκνα ἐν τῇ ἀληθείᾳ περιπατοῦντα.

records.literal_gloss: Greater than these not I have joy, that I hear my children in the truth walking.

en.L: Greater joy than these [things] I do not have: that I hear [that] my children are walking in the truth.
en.B: No joy of mine is greater than this: to hear that my children are walking in the truth.
en.R: Nothing brings me more joy than hearing that my children are living by the truth.

es.L: Mayor alegría que estas [cosas] no tengo: oír que mis hijos andan en la verdad.
es.B: Ninguna alegría es para mí más grande que esta: enterarme de que mis hijos andan en la verdad.
es.R: Nada me da más alegría que oír que mis hijos viven según la verdad.

fr.L: De joie plus grande que celles-ci, je n’en ai pas : entendre [dire] que mes enfants marchent dans la vérité.
fr.B: Je n’ai pas de plus grande joie que d’apprendre que mes enfants marchent dans la vérité.
fr.R: Rien ne me donne plus de joie que d’apprendre que mes enfants vivent selon la vérité.

sw.L: Furaha kubwa kuliko haya sina: kwamba nisikie watoto wangu wanatembea katika kweli.
sw.B: Hakuna furaha yangu iliyo kubwa kuliko hii: kusikia kwamba watoto wangu wanaishi katika kweli.
sw.R: Hakuna kitu kinachonipa furaha zaidi kuliko kusikia kwamba watoto wangu wanaishi kwa kufuata kweli.

ko.L: 내 자녀들이 진리 안에서 걷고 있다는 것을 듣는 것보다 더 큰 기쁨이 나에게는 없습니다.
ko.B: 내 자녀들이 진리 안에서 살고 있다는 소식을 듣는 것보다 더 큰 기쁨은 나에게 없습니다.
ko.R: 내 자녀들이 진리대로 살고 있다는 소식을 듣는 것보다 나를 더 기쁘게 하는 일은 없습니다.

vi.L: Tôi không có niềm vui nào lớn hơn điều này: nghe rằng con cái tôi đang bước đi trong chân lý.
vi.B: Không có niềm vui nào lớn hơn đối với tôi bằng được nghe rằng con cái tôi đang bước đi trong chân lý.
vi.R: Không gì làm tôi vui hơn là được nghe rằng con cái tôi đang sống theo chân lý.

pt.L: Não tenho alegria maior do que estas: ouvir que os meus filhos andam na verdade.
pt.B: Nenhuma alegria minha é maior do que esta: ouvir que os meus filhos andam na verdade.
pt.R: Nada me dá mais alegria do que ouvir que os meus filhos estão vivendo de acordo com a verdade.

am.L: ልጆቼ በእውነት እንደሚመላለሱ ከምሰማው ከዚህ የሚበልጥ ደስታ የለኝም።
am.B: ልጆቼ በእውነት እንደሚመላለሱ ከመስማት የሚበልጥ ደስታ የለኝም።
am.R: ልጆቼ በእውነት እንደሚኖሩ ከመስማት የበለጠ የሚያስደስተኝ ምንም ነገር የለም።

decisions.choice: no greater joy: the joy of hearing, stated after it
decisions.reason: μειζοτέραν is a comparative with a second comparative ending added, a form that adds emphasis. "These things" points forward to the clause after it: hearing that his children walk in the truth is the greatest joy he has.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: joy
alternatives: Greater grace than this I do not have
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads χαράν ("joy"). A few manuscripts, Codex Vaticanus among them, read χάριν ("grace" or "favor"), a word that differs by one letter. "Joy" fits the elder's "I rejoiced" in verse 3 and is read by most manuscripts. Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus before the sentence is marked meaning reviewed.

decisions.choice: my children: believers in the elder's care, whom he treats as a father
decisions.reason: The elder speaks of believers in his care, perhaps those who came to faith through him, as his children; Gaius is clearly one of them. The word is neuter and covers men and women. 1 John speaks to its readers in the same way (2:1, 12, 28).

decisions.choice: living by the truth
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom "walk" (see the note on verse 3).

source.text: Ἀγαπητέ, πιστὸν ποιεῖς ὃ ἐὰν ἐργάσῃ εἰς τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς καὶ τοῦτο ξένους, οἳ ἐμαρτύρησάν σου τῇ ἀγάπῃ ἐνώπιον ἐκκλησίας, οὓς καλῶς ποιήσεις προπέμψας ἀξίως τοῦ θεοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: Beloved, faithful [thing] you do whatever you work for the brothers and this strangers, \v 6 who testified of you to the love before [the] church, whom well you will do having sent forward worthily of the God;

en.L: Beloved, you are doing a faithful [thing] in whatever you do for the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, and that [though they are] strangers, \v 6 who testified to your love before [the] church; you will do well to send them forward in a manner worthy of God.
en.B: Dear friend, you are acting faithfully in all you do for the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, strangers though they are to you. \v 6 They have testified before the church to your love. You will do well to supply them for the next stage of their journey in a manner worthy of God.
en.R: Dear friend, you are being faithful when you help the believers who travel here, even though you never met them before. \v 6 They told the church about your love. Please give them what they need for the rest of their journey. Do it in a way that fits the God they serve.

es.L: Amado, haces [algo] fiel en todo lo que haces por los hermanos, y eso [siendo] forasteros, \v 6 los cuales dieron testimonio de tu amor delante de [la] iglesia; harás bien en encaminarlos de una manera digna de Dios.
es.B: Querido amigo, actúas con fidelidad en todo lo que haces por los hermanos, aunque sean forasteros para ti. \v 6 Ellos han dado testimonio de tu amor delante de la iglesia. Harás bien en proveerles lo necesario para la siguiente etapa de su viaje, de una manera digna de Dios.
es.R: Querido amigo, eres fiel cuando ayudas a los creyentes que viajan por aquí, aunque nunca los habías conocido. \v 6 Ellos le contaron a la iglesia de tu amor. Por favor, dales lo que necesiten para el resto de su viaje. Hazlo de una manera digna del Dios a quien sirven.

fr.L: Bien-aimé, tu fais œuvre fidèle en tout ce que tu accomplis pour les {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, et cela [alors qu’ils sont] des étrangers, \v 6 qui ont rendu témoignage à ton amour devant l’église ; tu feras bien de les mettre en route d’une manière digne de Dieu.
fr.B: Cher ami, tu agis fidèlement dans tout ce que tu fais pour les {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, alors qu’ils sont pour toi des étrangers. \v 6 Ils ont rendu témoignage de ton amour devant l’église. Tu feras bien de leur fournir ce qu’il faut pour la suite de leur voyage, d’une manière digne de Dieu.
fr.R: Cher ami, tu es fidèle quand tu aides les croyants qui passent chez toi en voyage, même si tu ne les avais jamais rencontrés. \v 6 Ils ont parlé de ton amour à l’église. S’il te plaît, donne-leur ce dont ils ont besoin pour la suite de leur voyage. Fais-le d’une manière qui convient au Dieu qu’ils servent.

sw.L: Mpendwa, unatenda [jambo la] uaminifu katika lolote unalowafanyia ndugu, na hilo [ingawa ni] wageni, \v 6 ambao walishuhudia upendo wako mbele ya kanisa; utafanya vizuri kuwasindikiza [safarini] kwa namna inayomstahili Mungu.
sw.B: Rafiki mpendwa, unatenda kwa uaminifu katika yote unayowafanyia ndugu, ingawa ni wageni kwako. \v 6 Wameshuhudia upendo wako mbele ya kanisa. Utafanya vizuri ukiwapa mahitaji yao kwa ajili ya hatua inayofuata ya safari yao, kwa namna inayomstahili Mungu.
sw.R: Rafiki mpendwa, unaonyesha uaminifu unapowasaidia waamini wanaosafiri kupita huko, ingawa hukuwa umewahi kuwaona kabla. \v 6 Wamelieleza kanisa habari za upendo wako. Tafadhali wape wanachohitaji kwa safari iliyobaki. Fanya hivyo kwa namna inayomfaa Mungu wanayemtumikia.

ko.L: 사랑하는 이여, 당신이 {{gender:형제자매|형제}}들에게, 그것도 나그네들에게 하는 일은 무엇이든지 신실한 일입니다. \v 6 그들은 교회 앞에서 당신의 사랑에 대해 증언하였습니다. 당신이 하나님께 합당하게 그들을 보내 준다면 잘하는 일일 것입니다.
ko.B: 사랑하는 친구여, 당신은 {{gender:형제자매|형제}}들을 위해 하는 모든 일에서 신실하게 행하고 있습니다. 그들은 당신에게 낯선 사람들인데도 그렇게 합니다. \v 6 그들은 교회 앞에서 당신의 사랑을 증언했습니다. 하나님께 합당하게 그들이 다음 길을 떠날 수 있도록 필요한 것을 마련해 준다면 잘하는 일일 것입니다.
ko.R: 사랑하는 친구여, 당신은 이곳을 다니는 믿음의 식구들을 도울 때 신실하게 행하고 있습니다. 당신이 그들을 전에 만난 적이 없는데도 그렇게 합니다. \v 6 그들은 교회에 당신의 사랑에 대해 말했습니다. 그들이 남은 여행을 할 수 있도록 필요한 것을 주십시오. 그들이 섬기는 하나님께 어울리게 그렇게 해 주십시오.

vi.L: Hỡi anh yêu dấu, anh làm một việc trung tín trong mọi điều anh làm cho {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}}, mà lại là những người khách lạ, \v 6 là những người đã làm chứng về tình yêu thương của anh trước Hội Thánh; anh sẽ làm tốt nếu tiễn họ lên đường cách xứng đáng với Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.B: Anh yêu dấu, anh đang làm cách trung tín mọi điều anh làm cho {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}}, dù họ là những người xa lạ với anh. \v 6 Họ đã làm chứng trước Hội Thánh về tình yêu thương của anh. Anh sẽ làm một việc tốt nếu cung cấp cho họ những gì cần cho chặng đường kế tiếp, cách xứng đáng với Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.R: Anh thân mến, anh đang tỏ ra trung tín khi giúp đỡ những tín hữu đi đường đến đây, dù trước đó anh chưa từng gặp họ. \v 6 Họ đã kể cho Hội Thánh nghe về tình yêu thương của anh. Xin anh hãy cung cấp cho họ những gì họ cần cho phần còn lại của chuyến đi. Hãy làm điều đó cho xứng với Đức Chúa Trời mà họ đang phục vụ.

pt.L: Amado, você faz [algo] fiel em tudo o que fizer pelos {{gender:irmãos e irmãs|irmãos}}, e isso [sendo eles] desconhecidos, \v 6 os quais deram testemunho do seu amor diante da igreja; você fará bem em encaminhá-los de modo digno de Deus.
pt.B: Querido amigo, você age com fidelidade em tudo o que faz pelos {{gender:irmãos e irmãs|irmãos}}, mesmo sendo eles desconhecidos para você. \v 6 Eles deram testemunho do seu amor diante da igreja. Você fará bem em dar a eles o necessário para a próxima etapa da viagem, de um modo digno de Deus.
pt.R: Querido amigo, você está sendo fiel quando ajuda {{gender:os irmãos e irmãs na fé|os irmãos na fé}} que viajam por aí, mesmo sem nunca ter conhecido essas pessoas antes. \v 6 Elas contaram à igreja sobre o seu amor. Por favor, dê a elas o que precisam para o resto da viagem. Faça isso de um jeito que combine com o Deus a quem elas servem.

am.L: የተወደድክ ሆይ፣ {{gender:ለወንድሞችና ለእኅቶች|ለወንድሞች}}፣ ይህንም እንግዶች ሆነው ሳሉ፣ የምታደርገውን ሁሉ በታማኝነት ታደርጋለህ፤ \v 6 እነርሱም በቤተ ክርስቲያን ፊት ስለ ፍቅርህ መሰከሩ፤ ለእግዚአብሔር እንደሚገባ አድርገህ ብትሸኛቸው መልካም ታደርጋለህ።
am.B: ወዳጄ ሆይ፣ {{gender:ለወንድሞችና ለእኅቶች|ለወንድሞች}} ምንም እንግዶች ቢሆኑብህም፣ የምታደርግላቸው ሁሉ የታማኝነት ሥራ ነው። \v 6 እነርሱ በቤተ ክርስቲያን ፊት ስለ ፍቅርህ መስክረዋል። ለጉዞአቸው የሚያስፈልጋቸውን አሟልተህ ለእግዚአብሔር በሚገባ መንገድ ብትሸኛቸው መልካም ታደርጋለህ።
am.R: ውድ ወዳጄ፣ ወደዚህ የሚጓዙትን አማኞች ከዚህ በፊት ባታውቃቸውም ስትረዳቸው ታማኝነትህን ታሳያለህ። \v 6 እነርሱ ለቤተ ክርስቲያን ስለ ፍቅርህ ነገሩ። እባክህ ለቀረው ጉዞአቸው የሚያስፈልጋቸውን ስጣቸው። ለሚያገለግሉት አምላክ በሚገባ መንገድ አድርገው።

decisions.choice: hospitality to traveling believers
decisions.reason: Christian teachers and messengers travelled from town to town, and they depended on believers to give them lodging and to help them on their way. Inns were few and had a poor name. To welcome them was a recognized duty of the churches (Romans 12:13; Hebrews 13:2; 1 Peter 4:9). An early Christian manual, the Didache (chapters 11-12), gives rules for receiving such travelers, and 2 John 10-11 warns against receiving those who bring false teaching. These brothers had been strangers to Gaius until they came, yet he received them.

decisions.choice: you do a faithful thing: what you do is an act of faithfulness
alternatives: you act as a believer should
decisions.reason: πιστὸν ποιεῖς means that Gaius's care for these travelers is faithful: loyal to the truth and true to what a believer is. It is the conduct of someone who can be relied on. The relative clause with ἐὰν and the aorist covers whatever he has done for them, or may do.

decisions.choice: and that, strangers: and all the more since they are strangers
decisions.reason: καὶ τοῦτο ("and this") adds a further point: they were strangers to him, which makes his kindness the more notable.

decisions.choice: before the church: in a meeting of the elder's church
decisions.reason: The travelers had come back and reported to the church where the elder was, at a gathering of believers. The noun has no article, which can mean "before a church gathering".

decisions.choice: you will do well: a polite way of asking
decisions.reason: καλῶς ποιήσεις ("you will do well") was a common courteous form of request in Greek letters, much like "please" or "kindly" (compare Acts 10:33; Philippians 4:14). It also commends the act as good.

decisions.choice: send them forward: equip them for the next stage of the journey
alternatives: send them off, see them on their way
decisions.reason: προπέμπω meant more than saying goodbye. It was to provide what a traveler needed for the road, such as food, money and sometimes companions (Acts 15:3; Romans 15:24; 1 Corinthians 16:6, 11; Titus 3:13).

decisions.choice: worthy of God: in a way that fits God, whose work they do
decisions.reason: Believers are to live "worthy of God" (1 Thessalonians 2:12; compare Colossians 1:10). These travelers are on God's work (verse 7), so the help Gaius gives them should be such as God deserves: generous, not grudging.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The travelers are fellow believers; the plural covers men and women, though the text does not tell us who these particular travelers were. Readable says "the believers", which needs no setting.

decisions.choice: supply them for the next stage of their journey
decisions.reason: Balanced says what the verb involved (meaning decision m6). "Send them on their way" would sound like a farewell only.

decisions.choice: who travel here; Please give them what they need; that fits the God they serve
alternatives: in a way worthy of God
decisions.reason: Readable says that the brothers are travelers (verse 7), turns the polite request into "please" (meaning decision m5), and explains "worthy of God" (meaning decision m7). "The God they serve" makes explicit a link the Greek leaves to verse 7.

decisions.choice: encaminarlos (L); proveerles lo necesario para la siguiente etapa de su viaje (B)
decisions.reason: The verb means equipping travellers for the next stage of their journey (m6). "Encaminar" (set someone on the way) keeps the single verb at Literal; "despedir" would only say goodbye. Balanced spells out the help, as the English Balanced does.

decisions.choice: l’église, lowercase, for the congregation (verses 6, 9, 10) (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: A local gathering of believers (m4), so lowercase, as the style guide sets for one congregation.

decisions.choice: kuwasindikiza [safarini] (L); ukiwapa mahitaji yao (B)
decisions.reason: The verb means equipping travellers for the next stage of their journey (m6). "Kuwasindikiza" (to see them on their way) keeps a single verb at Literal; "kuwaaga" would only say goodbye. Balanced spells out the help, as the English Balanced does.

decisions.choice: "나그네" (L), "낯선 사람" (B), "전에 만난 적이 없는" (R) for strangers; "교회" for the church; "보내 주다" (L), "다음 길을 떠날 수 있도록 ... 마련해 주다" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The strangers are travelling believers Gaius had not met before (meaning decision on hospitality). "교회" at every level for the church. "Send them forward" means equip them for the next stage of the journey (meaning decision), which Balanced and Readable say, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "tiễn họ lên đường" (L); "cung cấp ... cho chặng đường kế tiếp" (B)
decisions.reason: To send forward is to equip travellers for the next stage of the journey (m6), more than seeing them off. Literal keeps the picture of sending them on their way; Balanced and Readable say what is meant.

decisions.choice: encaminhá-los
decisions.reason: The verb means equipping travelers for the road, not only saying goodbye (meaning decision m6). "Encaminhar" says helping someone on his way; Balanced and Readable spell out the provision, as the English does.

decisions.choice: ብትሸኛቸው መልካም ታደርጋለህ (you will do well to send them on, L, B), with ለጉዞአቸው የሚያስፈልጋቸውን አሟልተህ (supplying what they need for their journey, B); እባክህ ... ስጣቸው (please give them, R)
decisions.reason: "መሸኘት" is to see a guest off on the road, which in Ethiopian custom includes giving them what they need for the way (meaning decision m6). "You will do well" is a polite request (m5), and Amharic "መልካም ታደርጋለህ" is said the same way; Readable makes it a plain "please".

source.text: ὑπὲρ γὰρ τοῦ ὀνόματος ἐξῆλθον μηδὲν λαμβάνοντες ἀπὸ τῶν ἐθνικῶν.

records.literal_gloss: On behalf of for the name they went out nothing receiving from the Gentiles.

en.L: For on behalf of the Name they went out, receiving nothing from the Gentiles.
en.B: They set out for the sake of the Name, and they take nothing from the pagans.
en.R: They started on their journey for the sake of the name of Jesus, and they do not accept anything from people who are not believers.

es.L: Porque en favor del Nombre salieron, sin recibir nada de los gentiles.
es.B: Se pusieron en camino por causa del Nombre, y no aceptan nada de los paganos.
es.R: Ellos emprendieron su viaje por causa del nombre de Jesús, y no aceptan nada de la gente que no cree.

fr.L: Car pour le Nom ils sont partis, ne recevant rien des nations.
fr.B: Ils se sont mis en route pour le Nom, et ils n’acceptent rien des païens.
fr.R: Ils sont partis en voyage pour le nom de Jésus, et ils n’acceptent rien des gens qui ne sont pas croyants.

sw.L: Kwa maana kwa ajili ya Jina waliondoka, wakiwa hawapokei chochote kutoka kwa watu wa mataifa.
sw.B: Walianza safari kwa ajili ya Jina, nao hawapokei chochote kutoka kwa wapagani.
sw.R: Walianza safari yao kwa ajili ya jina la Yesu, nao hawakubali kitu chochote kutoka kwa watu wasioamini.

ko.L: 그들은 그 이름을 위하여 떠났고, 이방 사람들에게서 아무것도 받지 않습니다.
ko.B: 그들은 그 이름을 위해 길을 떠났고, 믿지 않는 이방 사람들에게서는 아무것도 받지 않습니다.
ko.R: 그들은 예수님의 이름을 위해 여행을 시작했고, 믿지 않는 사람들에게서는 아무것도 받지 않습니다.

vi.L: Vì họ đã ra đi vì Danh ấy, không nhận gì từ các dân ngoại.
vi.B: Họ đã lên đường vì Danh ấy, và không nhận gì từ những người ngoại đạo.
vi.R: Họ đã bắt đầu chuyến đi vì danh Đức Giê-xu, và họ không nhận bất cứ điều gì từ những người không tin.

pt.L: Pois por causa do Nome saíram, sem receber nada dos pagãos.
pt.B: Eles partiram por causa do Nome e não aceitam nada dos pagãos.
pt.R: Eles começaram a viagem por causa do nome de Jesus, e não aceitam nada das pessoas que não creem.

am.L: ስለ ስሙ ወጥተዋልና፤ ከአሕዛብ ምንም ሳይቀበሉ።
am.B: እነርሱ የወጡት ስለ ስሙ ነው፤ ከአሕዛብም ምንም አይቀበሉም።
am.R: እነርሱ ጉዞአቸውን የጀመሩት ስለ ኢየሱስ ስም ነው፤ አማኞች ካልሆኑ ሰዎችም ምንም ነገር አይቀበሉም።

decisions.choice: the Name: the name of Jesus Christ, and so Christ himself
decisions.reason: "The Name" with no further word stands for the one who bears it. In the New Testament the apostles suffer "for the Name" (Acts 5:41) and believe "in his name" (1 John 3:23; 5:13); in 1 John 2:12 sins are forgiven "on account of his name". Jesus is the most likely referent; in Jewish usage "the Name" could also stand for God.

decisions.choice: went out: set out as messengers of the gospel
decisions.reason: ἐξέρχομαι is used of going out on a mission (Acts 15:40; compare 1 John 4:1 for false prophets who "have gone out"). They were traveling teachers or missionaries.

decisions.choice: the Gentiles: people who are not believers, pagans
decisions.reason: ἐθνικός is literally "belonging to the nations". In Matthew 5:47, 6:7 and 18:17 it means people outside God's people, and the same holds here: the people among whom the missionaries worked, who did not yet believe. It does not set Jewish against non-Jewish believers.

decisions.choice: receiving nothing: their settled practice
alternatives: they had received nothing (a mere fact)
decisions.reason: The present participle with μηδὲν describes their policy: they did not take support from those they preached to, so that no one could say they preached for gain (compare 1 Thessalonians 2:5-9; 1 Corinthians 9:12, 18). That is why believers must support them (verse 8).

decisions.choice: Gentiles (Literal); pagans (Balanced); people who are not believers (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Gentiles" shows the Greek word; "pagans" gives its sense here (meaning decision m3), as 1 Peter 4:3 does at Balanced. Readable says it in plain words.

decisions.choice: the name of Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus, the most likely referent (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: les nations (L); les païens (B); des gens qui ne sont pas croyants (R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means people who are not believers (m3), not non-Jews as such, so Balanced follows the English "pagans" rather than the style guide's "non-Juifs"; Literal keeps "les nations" as the style guide sets.

decisions.choice: "그 이름" (L, B); "예수님의 이름" (R); "이방 사람들" (L, B)
decisions.reason: The Name is the name of Jesus Christ, and so Christ himself (meaning decision, uncertain); Readable names him, as the English Readable does. The Gentiles here are people who are not believers (meaning decision), which Balanced adds to "이방 사람".

decisions.choice: "Danh ấy", capitalised (L, B), for "the Name"; "danh Đức Giê-xu" (R)
decisions.reason: The Name is the name of Jesus Christ, and so Christ himself (m1, uncertain); Vietnamese capitalises it, as the English does, so it is read as a title.

decisions.choice: os pagãos (L, B); as pessoas que não creem (R)
decisions.reason: Style section 11 renders this word (as in Matthew 5:47) "os pagãos". Here it means people outside God's people, not non-Jews as against Jews (meaning decision m3), so even Literal does not say "gentios", which would suggest the Jewish/Gentile divide. Readable says it plainly, as the English does, without "crentes".

decisions.choice: ስለ ስሙ (for the sake of the Name, L, B), ስለ ኢየሱስ ስም (R); አሕዛብ (the Gentiles, L, B), አማኞች ካልሆኑ ሰዎች (people who are not believers, R)
decisions.reason: The English writes "the Name" with a capital for the name of Jesus Christ (meaning decision m1); Ethiopic has no capitals, so Literal and Balanced use the definite "ስሙ" (the name) and Readable names Jesus. "አሕዛብ" is the table's word; here it means pagans, people who are not believers (m3), which Readable says.

source.text: ἡμεῖς οὖν ὀφείλομεν ὑπολαμβάνειν τοὺς τοιούτους, ἵνα συνεργοὶ γινώμεθα τῇ ἀληθείᾳ.

records.literal_gloss: We therefore ought to support such [people], so that fellow workers we may become with the truth.

en.L: We therefore ought to support such [people], so that we may become fellow workers with the truth.
en.B: It is our duty, then, to take in and support such people, and so become fellow workers with the truth.
en.R: So we should welcome and help people like these. Then we share in their work for the truth.

es.L: Nosotros, pues, debemos sostener a [personas] tales, para que lleguemos a ser colaboradores de la verdad.
es.B: Por eso es nuestro deber recibir y sostener a personas así, y de este modo ser colaboradores de la verdad.
es.R: Así que debemos dar la bienvenida y ayudar a personas como estas. Así participamos en su trabajo por la verdad.

fr.L: Nous devons donc soutenir de telles [personnes], afin de devenir des collaborateurs de la vérité.
fr.B: C’est donc notre devoir d’accueillir et de soutenir de telles personnes, et de devenir ainsi des collaborateurs de la vérité.
fr.R: Nous devons donc accueillir et aider des gens comme eux. Alors nous prenons part à leur travail pour la vérité.

sw.L: Basi sisi tunawajibika kuwategemeza watu wa namna hiyo, ili tuwe washirika katika kazi ya kweli.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo ni wajibu wetu kuwakaribisha na kuwategemeza watu kama hao, na hivyo tuwe washirika katika kazi ya kweli.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo tunapaswa kuwakaribisha na kuwasaidia watu kama hawa. Hapo tunashiriki katika kazi yao kwa ajili ya kweli.

ko.L: 그러므로 우리는 이런 사람들을 맞아들여야 합니다. 그래서 우리가 진리를 위한 동역자가 되게 하려는 것입니다.
ko.B: 그러므로 우리는 이런 사람들을 맞아들이고 도와야 합니다. 그렇게 해서 우리는 진리를 위해 함께 일하는 사람이 됩니다.
ko.R: 그러니 우리는 이런 사람들을 반갑게 맞아들이고 도와야 합니다. 그러면 우리도 진리를 위한 그들의 일에 함께 참여하게 됩니다.

vi.L: Vậy chúng ta phải tiếp đãi những người như thế, để chúng ta trở nên người cùng làm việc với chân lý.
vi.B: Vậy bổn phận của chúng ta là tiếp đón và giúp đỡ những người như thế, để trở nên những người cùng làm việc cho chân lý.
vi.R: Vì vậy chúng ta nên tiếp đón và giúp đỡ những người như vậy. Khi đó chúng ta được dự phần vào công việc của họ cho chân lý.

pt.L: Nós, portanto, devemos acolher tais [pessoas], para que nos tornemos colaboradores da verdade.
pt.B: É nosso dever, então, receber e sustentar pessoas assim, e desse modo nos tornar colaboradores da verdade.
pt.R: Por isso devemos receber e ajudar pessoas como essas. Assim participamos do trabalho delas pela verdade.

am.L: እኛም ስለዚህ ለእውነት አብረን ሠራተኞች እንሆን ዘንድ እንደነዚህ ያሉትን ልንደግፍ ይገባናል።
am.B: እንግዲህ እንደነዚህ ያሉትን ሰዎች ተቀብለን ልንረዳቸው ይገባናል፤ በዚህም ለእውነት አብረን ሠራተኞች እንሆናለን።
am.R: ስለዚህ እንደነዚህ ያሉትን ሰዎች ተቀብለን ልንረዳቸው ይገባል። ያን ጊዜ ለእውነት በሚሠሩት ሥራ ተካፋዮች እንሆናለን።

decisions.choice: support: receive as guests and provide for
decisions.reason: ὑπολαμβάνω means to take up or receive, and so to receive a guest and provide for him. It is chosen in contrast to the missionaries, who would "receive" (λαμβάνω) nothing from pagans (verse 7).

decisions.choice: we ought: an obligation on believers
decisions.reason: ἡμεῖς is emphatic: we believers, as against the pagans of verse 7. ὀφείλω means "to owe": this is a duty, not a mere kindness.

decisions.choice: fellow workers with the truth: working together with others for the truth
alternatives: fellow workers with the missionaries, for the truth
decisions.reason: The dative "to the truth" can mean that believers work together with the missionaries for the truth, or that they work alongside the truth itself, as if the truth were at work in the world and they joined it. The second reading may be meant: in verse 12 the truth itself also testifies. Either way, those who support the messengers share in their work.

decisions.choice: take in and support
decisions.reason: Balanced puts both parts of the verb into words: hospitality and provision (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: Then we share in their work for the truth.
alternatives: Then we become fellow workers with the truth.
decisions.reason: Readable gives the first sense of meaning decision m3, which is the easier one for a new reader. Literal and Balanced keep the open phrase.

decisions.choice: washirika katika kazi ya kweli
decisions.reason: The phrase most likely means working together with others for the truth (m3). "Washirika katika kazi ya kweli" (partners in the work of the truth) keeps that reading plain and leaves the truth as the cause served.

decisions.choice: "진리를 위한 동역자" (L); "진리를 위해 함께 일하는 사람" (B)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the phrase as working together with others for the truth, and footnotes the reading "fellow workers with the truth". "동역자" (co-worker) is the established church word; Balanced says it plainly.

source.text: Ἔγραψά τι τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ· ἀλλ’ ὁ φιλοπρωτεύων αὐτῶν Διοτρέφης οὐκ ἐπιδέχεται ἡμᾶς.

records.literal_gloss: I wrote something to the church; but the [one] loving to be first of them Diotrephes not receives us.

en.L: I wrote something to the church; but Diotrephes, who loves to be first among them, does not receive us.
en.B: I wrote a few lines to the church, but Diotrephes, who loves to be first among them, refuses to receive us.
en.R: I wrote a short letter to the church. But Diotrephes loves to be the most important person among them, and he will not accept us.

es.L: Escribí algo a la iglesia; pero Diótrefes, que ama ser el primero entre ellos, no nos recibe.
es.B: Escribí unas líneas a la iglesia, pero Diótrefes, que ama ser el primero entre ellos, se niega a recibirnos.
es.R: Escribí una carta breve a la iglesia. Pero a Diótrefes le encanta ser la persona más importante entre ellos, y no nos acepta.

fr.L: J’ai écrit quelque chose à l’église ; mais Diotrèphe, qui aime être le premier parmi eux, ne nous reçoit pas.
fr.B: J’ai écrit quelques mots à l’église, mais Diotrèphe, qui aime être le premier parmi eux, refuse de nous recevoir.
fr.R: J’ai écrit une petite lettre à l’église. Mais Diotrèphe aime être le plus important parmi eux, et il ne veut pas nous accepter.

sw.L: Nililiandikia kanisa jambo fulani; lakini Diotrefe, anayependa kuwa wa kwanza kati yao, hatupokei.
sw.B: Nililiandikia kanisa maneno machache, lakini Diotrefe, anayependa kuwa wa kwanza kati yao, anakataa kutupokea.
sw.R: Niliandika barua fupi kwa kanisa. Lakini Diotrefe anapenda kuwa mtu mkuu kuliko wote kati yao, naye hatukubali.

ko.L: 내가 교회에 몇 자 써 보냈습니다. 그러나 그들 가운데 으뜸이 되기를 좋아하는 디오드레베가 우리를 받아들이지 않습니다.
ko.B: 내가 교회에 몇 자 적어 보냈습니다. 그러나 그들 가운데서 첫째가 되기를 좋아하는 디오드레베가 우리를 받아들이지 않습니다.
ko.R: 나는 교회에 짧은 편지를 보냈습니다. 그러나 디오드레베는 그들 가운데서 가장 높은 사람이 되기를 좋아하고, 우리를 받아들이려고 하지 않습니다.

vi.L: Tôi đã viết vài điều cho Hội Thánh; nhưng Đi-ô-trép, là người thích đứng đầu giữa họ, không tiếp nhận chúng tôi.
vi.B: Tôi đã viết mấy dòng cho Hội Thánh, nhưng Đi-ô-trép, là người thích đứng đầu giữa họ, không chịu tiếp nhận chúng tôi.
vi.R: Tôi đã viết một lá thư ngắn cho Hội Thánh. Nhưng Đi-ô-trép thích làm người quan trọng nhất giữa họ, và ông ta không chịu chấp nhận chúng tôi.

pt.L: Escrevi algo à igreja; mas Diótrefes, que gosta de ser o primeiro entre eles, não nos recebe.
pt.B: Escrevi umas poucas linhas à igreja, mas Diótrefes, que gosta de ser o primeiro entre eles, se recusa a nos receber.
pt.R: Escrevi uma carta curta para a igreja. Mas Diótrefes adora ser a pessoa mais importante entre eles, e ele não nos aceita.

am.L: ለቤተ ክርስቲያን አንድ ነገር ጻፍኩ፤ ነገር ግን ከእነርሱ መካከል መቀደም የሚወድ ዲዮጥራጢስ አይቀበለንም።
am.B: ለቤተ ክርስቲያን ጥቂት ጻፍኩ፤ ነገር ግን በመካከላቸው የበላይ መሆን የሚወድ ዲዮጥራጢስ ሊቀበለን እንቢ ብሏል።
am.R: ለቤተ ክርስቲያን አጭር ደብዳቤ ጻፍኩ። ነገር ግን ዲዮጥራጢስ በመካከላቸው ከሁሉ የሚበልጥ ሰው መሆን ይወዳል፤ እኛንም አይቀበለንም።

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: I wrote something
alternatives: I would have written to the church
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads Ἔγραψά τι ("I wrote something"). Some manuscripts read "I would have written" (adding ἄν), and some later ones "I wrote to you" or leave out "something". The change to "I would have written" may have arisen because copyists were uneasy that a letter of the elder had been ignored or lost. Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus before the sentence is marked meaning reviewed.

decisions.choice: the letter to the church: a letter we do not have
decisions.reason: "Something" suggests a brief letter. It has not survived, unless it is one we know: some have thought of 2 John, but 2 John is about false teachers, not about hospitality or Diotrephes. Diotrephes seems to have kept it from having any effect. The church is apparently Gaius's own congregation or one near him.

decisions.choice: who loves to be first: who wants first place for himself
alternatives: who likes to put himself forward
decisions.reason: φιλοπρωτεύω is found nowhere else in the New Testament. It joins "loving" to "being first", and describes ambition: a man who likes to lead and to have the chief place. A related verb is used of Christ, who is to have first place in everything (Colossians 1:18); Jesus taught that whoever would be first must be the slave of all (Mark 10:44).

decisions.choice: Diotrephes: what the text says about him, and what it does not
decisions.reason: The letter says that Diotrephes had enough influence in that church to refuse the elder and his messengers, to speak against him, to refuse the traveling believers, to stop others from receiving them and to put such people out of the church (verse 10). It does not say what office he held, whether elder, host of the church in his house, or something else. It does not charge him with false teaching, as 2 John does its deceivers; the complaint is his ambition and conduct. Views that make him an early single bishop, or the leader of a doctrinal party, go beyond what the text says. His name was a Greek one.

decisions.choice: does not receive us: refuses the elder's authority and his messengers
decisions.reason: ἐπιδέχομαι means to receive or welcome. In verse 10 it is used of receiving the traveling believers as guests. Here "us" is the elder (and those with him): Diotrephes would not accept his letter or his authority, and would not welcome those he sent.

decisions.choice: a few lines
decisions.reason: The indefinite "something" points to a short letter (meaning decision m2); Balanced says so naturally.

decisions.choice: loves to be the most important person among them
decisions.reason: Readable explains "to be first" in plain words (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: "디오드레베"; "으뜸이 되기를 좋아하는" (L); "첫째가 되기를 좋아하는" (B)
decisions.reason: "디오드레베" is the established Protestant form. The meaning decision reads the word as one who wants first place for himself; Korean says that plainly without adding a title or office the text does not give.

decisions.choice: "Đi-ô-trép", "ông ta" (R) for Diotrephes; exclusive "chúng tôi" for the elder and his messengers
decisions.reason: Diotrephes is spoken of with disapproval, so Readable uses "ông ta", as the Vietnamese 2 Peter does for Balaam; the "us" he refuses is the elder and those he sends (m5), not Gaius, so it is exclusive.

decisions.choice: ዲዮጥራጢስ (Diotrephes), ድሜጥሮስ (Demetrius, verse 12); መቀደም የሚወድ (who loves to be first, L), የበላይ መሆን የሚወድ (B)
decisions.reason: The names are written as Amharic Bible readers know them. The Greek word is one compound, "loving to be first" (meaning decision m3); Literal keeps the picture of going first, and Balanced and Readable say he wants the highest place.

source.text: διὰ τοῦτο, ἐὰν ἔλθω, ὑπομνήσω αὐτοῦ τὰ ἔργα ἃ ποιεῖ, λόγοις πονηροῖς φλυαρῶν ἡμᾶς, καὶ μὴ ἀρκούμενος ἐπὶ τούτοις οὔτε αὐτὸς ἐπιδέχεται τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς καὶ τοὺς βουλομένους κωλύει καὶ ἐκ τῆς ἐκκλησίας ἐκβάλλει.

records.literal_gloss: Because of this, if I come, I will bring to mind of him the works which he does, with words evil talking nonsense [against] us, and not being content with these neither himself receives the brothers and those wishing he hinders and out of the church throws out.

en.L: Because of this, if I come, I will bring to mind his works that he is doing, talking nonsense against us with evil words; and not content with these [things], neither does he himself receive the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, and those who want [to] he hinders and throws [them] out of the church.
en.B: That is why, if I come, I will remind the church of what he is doing, spreading empty and wicked talk about us. And that is not enough for him: he will not receive the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} himself, he hinders those who want to receive them, and he drives them out of the church.
en.R: So if I come, I will remind everyone of what Diotrephes is doing. He says evil and foolish things about us. But that is not all. He will not welcome the traveling believers. When other people want to welcome them, he tries to stop them, and he throws them out of the church.

es.L: Por eso, si voy, traeré a la memoria las obras que él hace, diciendo contra nosotros disparates con palabras malvadas; y no satisfecho con eso, tampoco recibe él mismo a los hermanos, y a quienes quieren [hacerlo] se lo impide y [los] echa fuera de la iglesia.
es.B: Por eso, si voy, le recordaré a la iglesia lo que él está haciendo: anda diciendo de nosotros cosas vacías y malvadas. Y eso no le basta: él mismo no quiere recibir a los hermanos, impide a los que quieren recibirlos y los expulsa de la iglesia.
es.R: Así que, si voy, les recordaré a todos lo que Diótrefes está haciendo. Dice cosas malas y tontas acerca de nosotros. Pero eso no es todo. No quiere dar la bienvenida a los creyentes que viajan. Cuando otros quieren recibirlos, trata de impedírselo, y los echa de la iglesia.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi, si je viens, je rappellerai les œuvres qu’il fait, tenant contre nous des propos absurdes avec des paroles mauvaises ; et, non content de cela, lui-même ne reçoit pas les {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, et ceux qui le veulent, il les en empêche et [les] chasse de l’église.
fr.B: Voilà pourquoi, si je viens, je rappellerai à l’église ce qu’il fait : il répand sur nous des propos vides et méchants. Et cela ne lui suffit pas : lui-même ne reçoit pas les {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, il empêche ceux qui voudraient les recevoir de le faire, et il les chasse de l’église.
fr.R: Alors, si je viens, je rappellerai à tous ce que fait Diotrèphe. Il dit des choses méchantes et stupides sur nous. Mais ce n’est pas tout. Il refuse d’accueillir les croyants qui voyagent. Quand d’autres veulent les accueillir, il essaie de les en empêcher, et il les chasse de l’église.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo, nikija, nitazikumbusha kazi zake anazozifanya, akibwabwaja upuuzi dhidi yetu kwa maneno maovu; na asiporidhika na hayo, yeye mwenyewe hawapokei ndugu, na wale wanaotaka [kuwapokea] huwazuia na kuwafukuza kanisani.
sw.B: Ndiyo maana, nikija, nitalikumbusha kanisa mambo anayoyafanya, jinsi anavyoeneza maneno matupu na maovu juu yetu. Wala hilo halimtoshi: yeye mwenyewe hakubali kuwapokea ndugu, huwazuia wale wanaotaka kuwapokea, na kuwafukuza kanisani.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo nikija, nitawakumbusha wote mambo ambayo Diotrefe anafanya. Anasema mambo mabaya na ya kipumbavu juu yetu. Lakini si hayo tu. Hataki kuwakaribisha waamini wanaosafiri. Watu wengine wanapotaka kuwakaribisha, anajaribu kuwazuia, na anawafukuza kanisani.

ko.L: 그러므로 내가 가면, 그가 하는 일들을 기억나게 하겠습니다. 그는 악한 말로 우리를 헐뜯고, 그것으로도 만족하지 않아서, 자기도 {{gender:형제자매|형제}}들을 맞아들이지 않고, 맞아들이려는 사람들을 막고 교회에서 내쫓습니다.
ko.B: 그러므로 내가 가면, 그가 하는 일들을 교회에 드러내겠습니다. 그는 악하고 헛된 말로 우리를 헐뜯고 다닙니다. 그것으로도 모자라서, 자기도 {{gender:형제자매|형제}}들을 맞아들이지 않을 뿐 아니라, 맞아들이려는 사람들을 막고 교회에서 내쫓습니다.
ko.R: 그러니 내가 가면, 디오드레베가 하는 일을 모든 사람에게 다시 알리겠습니다. 그는 우리에 대해 악하고 터무니없는 말을 합니다. 그러나 그것이 다가 아닙니다. 그는 여행하는 믿음의 식구들을 맞아들이지 않습니다. 다른 사람들이 그들을 맞아들이려고 하면 막고, 그런 사람들을 교회에서 쫓아냅니다.

vi.L: Vì vậy, nếu tôi đến, tôi sẽ nhắc lại những việc người ấy đang làm, dùng những lời độc ác mà nói nhảm chống lại chúng tôi; và chưa thỏa mãn với những điều ấy, chính người ấy không tiếp đón {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}}, và những người muốn [tiếp đón] thì người ấy ngăn cản và đuổi [họ] ra khỏi Hội Thánh.
vi.B: Vì thế, nếu tôi đến, tôi sẽ nhắc cho Hội Thánh biết những việc người ấy đang làm: tung ra những lời nhảm nhí và độc ác về chúng tôi. Mà người ấy vẫn chưa thấy đủ: chính người ấy không tiếp đón {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}}, lại ngăn cản những người muốn tiếp đón họ, và đuổi những người ấy ra khỏi Hội Thánh.
vi.R: Vì vậy nếu tôi đến, tôi sẽ nhắc cho mọi người biết những gì Đi-ô-trép đang làm. Ông ta nói những điều xấu xa và vô lý về chúng tôi. Nhưng chưa hết. Ông ta không chịu tiếp đón các tín hữu đi đường. Khi người khác muốn tiếp đón họ, ông ta tìm cách ngăn cản, và ông ta đuổi họ ra khỏi Hội Thánh.

pt.L: Por isso, se eu for, lembrarei as obras que ele faz, falando contra nós tolices com palavras más; e, não contente com isso, nem ele mesmo recebe os {{gender:irmãos e irmãs|irmãos}}, e aos que querem [recebê-los] ele impede e [os] expulsa da igreja.
pt.B: É por isso que, se eu for, vou lembrar à igreja o que ele está fazendo, espalhando conversas vazias e maldosas a nosso respeito. E isso não lhe basta: ele mesmo não recebe os {{gender:irmãos e irmãs|irmãos}}, impede os que querem recebê-los e os expulsa da igreja.
pt.R: Por isso, se eu for, vou lembrar a todos o que Diótrefes está fazendo. Ele diz coisas más e tolas sobre nós. Mas isso não é tudo. Ele não recebe bem {{gender:os irmãos e irmãs na fé|os irmãos na fé}} que viajam. Quando outras pessoas querem recebê-los, ele tenta impedi-las e as expulsa da igreja.

am.L: ስለዚህ ብመጣ የሚያደርገውን ሥራውን አሳስባለሁ፤ በክፉ ቃላት በእኛ ላይ እየለፈለፈ፤ በዚህም ሳይበቃው እርሱ ራሱ {{gender:ወንድሞችንና እኅቶችን|ወንድሞችን}} አይቀበልም፤ ሊቀበሉ የሚፈልጉትንም ይከለክላል፤ ከቤተ ክርስቲያንም ያወጣቸዋል።
am.B: ስለዚህ ብመጣ የሚያደርገውን ለቤተ ክርስቲያን አስታውሳለሁ፤ ስለ እኛ ከንቱና ክፉ ወሬ ያወራል። ይህም አልበቃውም፤ እርሱ ራሱ {{gender:ወንድሞችንና እኅቶችን|ወንድሞችን}} አይቀበልም፤ ሊቀበሏቸው የሚፈልጉትንም ይከለክላል፤ ከቤተ ክርስቲያንም ያባርራቸዋል።
am.R: ስለዚህ ብመጣ ዲዮጥራጢስ የሚያደርገውን ለሁሉም አስታውሳለሁ። ስለ እኛ ክፉና የማይረባ ነገር ይናገራል። ይህ ብቻ አይደለም፤ የሚጓዙትን አማኞች አይቀበልም። ሌሎች ሊቀበሏቸው ሲፈልጉ ይከለክላቸዋል፤ ከቤተ ክርስቲያንም ያባርራቸዋል።

decisions.choice: if I come: a real intention, not a threat in doubt
decisions.reason: The elder plans to visit (verse 14). "If" leaves the timing to circumstances, not the intention.

decisions.choice: I will bring up his deeds: call public attention to them
alternatives: I will remember what he does
decisions.reason: ὑπομιμνῄσκω means to remind or bring to mind. When the elder comes, he will raise Diotrephes's conduct openly before the church, rather than let it pass.

decisions.choice: talking nonsense against us with evil words: malicious, baseless gossip
decisions.reason: φλυαρέω means to talk idly, to babble (the related adjective "gossips" is in 1 Timothy 5:13). The charges are empty, without substance, but the words are evil in intent.

decisions.choice: he hinders and throws out: what he does, or tries to do
alternatives: he tries to stop them and to put them out
decisions.reason: The present tenses describe his habit. They may also mean that he tries to stop and expel people, without saying how far he succeeded. "Those who want to" are church members who wished to receive the travelers.

decisions.choice: throws out of the church: excludes them from the gathering of believers
decisions.reason: To be put out of the church was to be shut out of its meetings and fellowship (compare John 9:22, 34, of the synagogue). The text does not say by what means Diotrephes did this: by authority of office, by influence, or by controlling the house where the church met.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The travelers of verses 5-8 are meant; the plural covers men and women. Readable says "the traveling believers", which needs no setting.

decisions.choice: remind the church
decisions.reason: Balanced says who is reminded: the deeds will be raised before the church (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: Diotrephes; the traveling believers
decisions.reason: Readable names the man and says who "the brothers" are, to keep the long sentence clear when it is broken up.

decisions.choice: "헐뜯다" for talking nonsense against us; "악하고 헛된 말" (B)
decisions.reason: The words mean malicious, baseless gossip (meaning decision); "헐뜯다" is the plain current word, as in James 4:11 and 1 Peter 2:1, and "폄론" is archaic.

decisions.choice: se eu for
decisions.reason: Portuguese says "ir" for going to where the hearer is, so the elder's planned visit to Gaius's church is "se eu for"; "se eu vier" would place the writer where the reader is.

source.text: Ἀγαπητέ, μὴ μιμοῦ τὸ κακὸν ἀλλὰ τὸ ἀγαθόν.

records.literal_gloss: Beloved, not imitate the evil but the good.

en.L: Beloved, do not imitate what is evil, but what is good.
en.B: Dear friend, do not copy what is bad, but what is good.
en.R: Dear friend, do not follow the example of what is evil. Follow the example of what is good.

es.L: Amado, no imites el mal, sino el bien.
es.B: Querido amigo, no copies lo que es malo, sino lo que es bueno.
es.R: Querido amigo, no sigas el ejemplo de lo que es malo. Sigue el ejemplo de lo que es bueno.

fr.L: Bien-aimé, n’imite pas ce qui est mal, mais ce qui est bien.
fr.B: Cher ami, n’imite pas le mal, mais le bien.
fr.R: Cher ami, ne suis pas l’exemple de ce qui est mal. Suis l’exemple de ce qui est bien.

sw.L: Mpendwa, usiige yaliyo mabaya, bali yaliyo mema.
sw.B: Rafiki mpendwa, usiige mabaya, bali uige mema.
sw.R: Rafiki mpendwa, usifuate mfano wa jambo lililo baya. Fuata mfano wa jambo lililo jema.

ko.L: 사랑하는 이여, 악한 것을 본받지 말고 선한 것을 본받으십시오.
ko.B: 사랑하는 친구여, 나쁜 것을 본받지 말고 선한 것을 본받으십시오.
ko.R: 사랑하는 친구여, 나쁜 것을 본받지 마십시오. 선한 것을 본받으십시오.

vi.L: Hỡi anh yêu dấu, chớ bắt chước điều ác, nhưng [hãy bắt chước] điều lành.
vi.B: Anh yêu dấu, đừng bắt chước điều xấu, nhưng hãy bắt chước điều tốt.
vi.R: Anh thân mến, đừng noi theo gương xấu. Hãy noi theo gương tốt.

pt.L: Amado, não imite o mal, mas o bem.
pt.B: Querido amigo, não imite o que é mau, mas o que é bom.
pt.R: Querido amigo, não siga o exemplo do que é mau. Siga o exemplo do que é bom.

am.L: የተወደድክ ሆይ፣ ክፉ የሆነውን አትምሰል፤ መልካም የሆነውን እንጂ።
am.B: ወዳጄ ሆይ፣ ክፉ የሆነውን ሳይሆን መልካም የሆነውን ምሰል።
am.R: ውድ ወዳጄ፣ ክፉ የሚያደርጉትን አትከተል። መልካም የሚያደርጉትን ተከተል።

decisions.choice: imitate: follow an example
decisions.reason: μιμέομαι is to follow the example of another (2 Thessalonians 3:7, 9; Hebrews 13:7). The words are neuter, "the evil" and "the good", but they come between the example of Diotrephes (verses 9-10) and the good report of Demetrius (verse 12), so the reader thinks of them.

decisions.choice: Beloved (Literal); Dear friend (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

decisions.choice: ክፉ የሆነውን (what is evil), not ክፉውን
decisions.reason: In 1 John "ክፉው" names the evil one, the devil. Here the Greek is a neuter, what is bad (meaning decision m1 speaks of following an example), so Amharic says "what is evil" to keep the two apart.

source.text: ὁ ἀγαθοποιῶν ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ ἐστιν· ὁ κακοποιῶν οὐχ ἑώρακεν τὸν θεόν.

records.literal_gloss: The [one] doing good from the God is; the [one] doing evil not has seen the God.

en.L: The one who does good is from God; the one who does evil has not seen God.
en.B: The person who does good is from God; the person who does evil has not seen God.
en.R: Those who do good belong to God. Those who do evil have never truly seen God.

es.L: El que hace el bien es de Dios; el que hace el mal no ha visto a Dios.
es.B: Quien hace el bien procede de Dios; quien hace el mal no ha visto a Dios.
es.R: Los que hacen el bien pertenecen a Dios. Los que hacen el mal nunca han visto de verdad a Dios.

fr.L: Celui qui fait le bien est de Dieu ; celui qui fait le mal n’a pas vu Dieu.
fr.B: Qui fait le bien vient de Dieu ; qui fait le mal n’a pas vu Dieu.
fr.R: Ceux qui font le bien appartiennent à Dieu. Ceux qui font le mal n’ont jamais vraiment vu Dieu.

sw.L: Anayetenda mema ametoka kwa Mungu; anayetenda mabaya hajamwona Mungu.
sw.B: Mtu anayetenda mema ametoka kwa Mungu; mtu anayetenda mabaya hajamwona Mungu.
sw.R: Watu wanaotenda mema ni wa Mungu. Watu wanaotenda mabaya hawajawahi kumwona Mungu kweli.

ko.L: 선을 행하는 사람은 하나님에게서 났고, 악을 행하는 사람은 하나님을 보지 못했습니다.
ko.B: 선을 행하는 사람은 하나님께 속한 사람이고, 악을 행하는 사람은 하나님을 본 적이 없습니다.
ko.R: 선한 일을 하는 사람들은 하나님께 속해 있습니다. 악한 일을 하는 사람들은 하나님을 한 번도 제대로 본 적이 없습니다.

vi.L: Người làm điều lành là từ Đức Chúa Trời; người làm điều ác thì chưa thấy Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.B: Người làm điều lành thì thuộc về Đức Chúa Trời; người làm điều ác thì chưa thấy Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.R: Những ai làm điều lành là thuộc về Đức Chúa Trời. Những ai làm điều ác thì chưa bao giờ thật sự thấy Đức Chúa Trời.

pt.L: Quem faz o bem é de Deus; quem faz o mal não viu a Deus.
pt.B: Quem pratica o bem é de Deus; quem pratica o mal não viu a Deus.
pt.R: Quem faz o bem pertence a Deus. Quem faz o mal nunca viu a Deus de verdade.

am.L: መልካም የሚያደርግ ከእግዚአብሔር ነው፤ ክፉ የሚያደርግ እግዚአብሔርን አላየም።
am.B: መልካም የሚያደርግ ሰው ከእግዚአብሔር ነው፤ ክፉ የሚያደርግ ሰው ግን እግዚአብሔርን አላየም።
am.R: መልካም የሚያደርጉ ሰዎች የእግዚአብሔር ናቸው። ክፉ የሚያደርጉ ሰዎች ግን እግዚአብሔርን በእውነት ከቶ አላዩትም።

decisions.choice: who does good, who does evil: a way of life
decisions.reason: The present participles describe what a person habitually does, as in 1 John 3:6-10.

decisions.choice: from God: born of God, belonging to God
decisions.reason: In 1 John to be "from God" is to have one's life from him and to belong to him (1 John 3:10; 4:4, 6; 5:19). Doing good shows it.

decisions.choice: has not seen God: has never known God
decisions.reason: No one has ever seen God with the eyes (John 1:18; 1 John 4:12, 20). To "see" him here is to perceive and know him by faith, as in 1 John 3:6, "has not seen him nor known him", and John 14:9. The perfect tense describes a seeing that would have lasting effect.

decisions.choice: belong to God; have never truly seen God
alternatives: are from God; have not seen God
decisions.reason: Readable says what "from God" means (meaning decision m2), as 1 John 3:10 does, and adds "truly" so that "seen" is not taken to mean seeing with the eyes (meaning decision m3).

source.text: Δημητρίῳ μεμαρτύρηται ὑπὸ πάντων καὶ ὑπὸ αὐτῆς τῆς ἀληθείας· καὶ ἡμεῖς δὲ μαρτυροῦμεν, καὶ οἶδας ὅτι ἡ μαρτυρία ἡμῶν ἀληθής ἐστιν.

records.literal_gloss: To Demetrius it has been testified by all and by itself the truth; and we also testify, and you know that the testimony of us true is.

en.L: To Demetrius it has been testified by all and by the truth itself; and we also testify, and you know that our testimony is true.
en.B: Everyone testifies in favor of Demetrius, and so does the truth itself. We too testify for him, and you know that our testimony is true.
en.R: Everyone speaks well of Demetrius, and the truth itself speaks for him, because his life matches it. We speak for him too, and you know that what we say is true.

es.L: A Demetrio se le ha dado testimonio por parte de todos y por parte de la verdad misma; y también nosotros damos testimonio, y sabes que verdadero es nuestro testimonio.
es.B: Demetrio cuenta con el testimonio favorable de todos, y de la verdad misma. También nosotros damos testimonio a su favor, y sabes que nuestro testimonio es verdadero.
es.R: Todos hablan bien de Demetrio, y la verdad misma habla a su favor, porque su vida está de acuerdo con ella. Nosotros también hablamos a su favor, y tú sabes que lo que decimos es verdad.

fr.L: À Démétrius témoignage a été rendu par tous et par la vérité elle-même ; et nous aussi, nous rendons témoignage, et tu sais que notre témoignage est vrai.
fr.B: Tout le monde rend un bon témoignage à Démétrius, et la vérité elle-même aussi. Nous aussi, nous lui rendons témoignage, et tu sais que notre témoignage est vrai.
fr.R: Tout le monde dit du bien de Démétrius, et la vérité elle-même parle en sa faveur, parce que sa vie est d’accord avec elle. Nous aussi, nous parlons en sa faveur, et tu sais que ce que nous disons est vrai.

sw.L: Kwa habari ya Demetrio, ushuhuda umetolewa na wote na kweli yenyewe pia; nasi pia tunatoa ushuhuda, na unafahamu kwamba ushuhuda wetu ni wa kweli.
sw.B: Kila mtu anamtolea Demetrio ushuhuda mzuri, na kweli yenyewe pia. Sisi nasi tunamtolea ushuhuda, nawe unajua kwamba ushuhuda wetu ni wa kweli.
sw.R: Kila mtu anasema mema juu ya Demetrio, na kweli yenyewe inamtetea, kwa sababu maisha yake yanapatana nayo. Sisi pia tunamtetea, nawe unajua kwamba tunayoyasema ni ya kweli.

ko.L: 데메드리오는 모든 사람에게서, 그리고 진리 자체에게서 증언을 받았습니다. 우리도 증언합니다. 그리고 당신은 우리의 증언이 참되다는 것을 압니다.
ko.B: 데메드리오에 대해서는 모든 사람이 좋게 증언하고, 진리 자체도 그를 위해 증언합니다. 우리도 그를 위해 증언합니다. 당신은 우리의 증언이 참되다는 것을 압니다.
ko.R: 모든 사람이 데메드리오를 좋게 말합니다. 그의 삶이 진리와 맞기 때문에 진리 자체도 그를 위해 말해 줍니다. 우리도 그를 위해 말합니다. 당신은 우리가 하는 말이 참되다는 것을 압니다.

vi.L: Đê-mê-triu đã được mọi người và chính chân lý làm chứng tốt; chúng tôi cũng làm chứng nữa, và anh biết rằng lời chứng của chúng tôi là thật.
vi.B: Mọi người đều làm chứng tốt về Đê-mê-triu, và chính chân lý cũng vậy. Chúng tôi cũng làm chứng cho anh ấy, và anh biết rằng lời chứng của chúng tôi là thật.
vi.R: Mọi người đều nói tốt về Đê-mê-triu, và chính chân lý cũng làm chứng cho anh ấy, vì đời sống anh ấy phù hợp với chân lý. Chúng tôi cũng làm chứng cho anh ấy, và anh biết rằng điều chúng tôi nói là thật.

pt.L: A Demétrio tem sido dado testemunho por todos e pela própria verdade; e nós também damos testemunho, e você sabe que o nosso testemunho é verdadeiro.
pt.B: Todos dão bom testemunho de Demétrio, e a própria verdade também. Nós também damos testemunho a favor dele, e você sabe que o nosso testemunho é verdadeiro.
pt.R: Todos falam bem de Demétrio, e a própria verdade fala a favor dele, porque a vida dele combina com ela. Nós também falamos a favor dele, e você sabe que o que dizemos é verdade.

am.L: ለድሜጥሮስ በሁሉም በእውነትም ራሱ ተመስክሮለታል፤ እኛም ደግሞ እንመሰክርለታለን፤ ምስክርነታችንም እውነት እንደ ሆነ ታውቃለህ።
am.B: ሁሉም ስለ ድሜጥሮስ በመልካም ይመሰክሩለታል፤ እውነት ራሱም ይመሰክርለታል። እኛም ደግሞ እንመሰክርለታለን፤ ምስክርነታችንም እውነት እንደ ሆነ ታውቃለህ።
am.R: ሁሉም ስለ ድሜጥሮስ መልካም ይናገራሉ፤ ሕይወቱ ከእውነት ጋር ስለሚስማማ እውነት ራሱ ይመሰክርለታል። እኛም ስለ እርሱ እንመሰክራለን፤ የምንናገረውም እውነት እንደ ሆነ ታውቃለህ።

decisions.choice: Demetrius: a believer commended to Gaius
decisions.reason: Demetrius was a common Greek name. This Demetrius is otherwise unknown; the text gives no ground for identifying him with the silversmith of Ephesus (Acts 19:24) or anyone else. The verse is a short letter of recommendation, like Romans 16:1-2. He may have carried this letter, or he may have been a traveling believer whom Gaius was asked to receive, perhaps one Diotrephes would not.

decisions.choice: the truth itself testifies: his life agrees with the truth
alternatives: the Spirit, who is the truth
decisions.reason: The truth testifies for him because he lives by it: his conduct speaks for itself. Some take "the truth" as the Spirit, whom 1 John 5:6 calls "the truth" and who testifies. The first is simpler in a letter where truth is what believers walk in (verses 3-4).

decisions.choice: you know that our testimony is true: as John 19:35 and 21:24
decisions.reason: The words recall the closing claims of John's Gospel that the witness's testimony is true (John 19:35; 21:24). "We" is the elder and those with him, adding a third witness to "all" and to the truth (compare Deuteronomy 19:15).

decisions.choice: has been testified: the testimony stands
decisions.reason: The perfect passive μεμαρτύρηται means that a good report has been given and holds good. The dative "to Demetrius" marks the one in whose favor it was given.

decisions.choice: Everyone testifies in favor of Demetrius
alternatives: Demetrius has received testimony from everyone
decisions.reason: Balanced turns the impersonal passive into an active sentence, as English prefers. Literal keeps the passive.

decisions.choice: speaks well of; speaks for him, because his life matches it; what we say
decisions.reason: Readable puts "testify" and "testimony" in plain words and says why the truth speaks for him (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: sabes que verdadero es nuestro testimonio (L); sabes que nuestro testimonio es verdadero (B)
decisions.reason: The words echo John 21:24 (m3), so they follow the Spanish of that verse at each level, with "dar testimonio" and "testimonio" as in John and 1 John.

decisions.choice: rendre témoignage, le témoignage (L, B); dire du bien, parler en sa faveur (R) (also verses 3, 6)
decisions.reason: The style guide's term for John's writings; Readable says it in plain words where the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: unafahamu (L), unajua (B) kwamba ushuhuda wetu ni wa kweli
decisions.reason: The words echo John 21:24 (m3), so they follow the Swahili of that verse at each level, with "ushuhuda" as in John and 1 John.

decisions.choice: "데메드리오"; "참되다" for true testimony, as in the Korean John 19:35 and 21:24
decisions.reason: "데메드리오" is the established Protestant form. The meaning decision hears an echo of John 19:35 and 21:24, so the same Korean "증언이 참되다" is used.

source.text: Πολλὰ εἶχον γράψαι σοι, ἀλλ’ οὐ θέλω διὰ μέλανος καὶ καλάμου σοι γράφειν·

records.literal_gloss: Many things I had to write to you, but not I want through ink and pen to you to write;

en.L: I had many things to write to you, but I do not want to write to you with ink and pen;
en.B: There is a great deal I could write to you, but I do not want to put it down in ink with a pen.
en.R: I have a lot more to tell you, but I do not want to do it in a letter.

es.L: Muchas cosas tenía para escribirte, pero no quiero escribirte por medio de tinta y cálamo.
es.B: Tengo mucho que podría escribirte, pero no quiero ponerlo por escrito con tinta y pluma.
es.R: Tengo mucho más que contarte, pero no quiero hacerlo en una carta.

fr.L: J’avais beaucoup de choses à t’écrire, mais je ne veux pas t’écrire avec l’encre et la plume ;
fr.B: J’aurais beaucoup de choses à t’écrire, mais je ne veux pas le faire avec l’encre et la plume.
fr.R: J’ai encore beaucoup de choses à te dire, mais je ne veux pas le faire dans une lettre.

sw.L: Mengi nilikuwa nayo ya kukuandikia, lakini sitaki kukuandikia [mambo hayo] kwa kutumia wino na kalamu.
sw.B: Kuna mengi ambayo ningeweza kukuandikia, lakini sitaki kuyaweka katika maandishi kwa wino na kalamu.
sw.R: Nina mambo mengi zaidi ya kukuambia, lakini sitaki kuyaandika katika barua.

ko.L: 내가 당신에게 쓸 것이 많았지만, 먹과 붓으로 당신에게 쓰고 싶지 않습니다.
ko.B: 당신에게 쓸 것이 많지만, 먹과 붓으로 적고 싶지는 않습니다.
ko.R: 당신에게 할 말이 아직 많지만, 편지로 쓰고 싶지는 않습니다.

vi.L: Tôi còn có nhiều điều để viết cho anh, nhưng tôi không muốn viết cho anh bằng mực và bút;
vi.B: Tôi còn nhiều điều có thể viết cho anh, nhưng tôi không muốn dùng bút mực để viết ra.
vi.R: Tôi còn nhiều điều muốn nói với anh, nhưng tôi không muốn viết trong thư.

pt.L: Eu tinha muitas coisas para escrever a você, mas não quero lhe escrever com tinta e pena;
pt.B: Há muita coisa que eu poderia escrever a você, mas não quero fazer isso com tinta e pena.
pt.R: Tenho muito mais coisas para contar a você, mas não quero fazer isso numa carta.

am.L: ብዙ የምጽፍልህ ነገር ነበረኝ፤ ነገር ግን በቀለምና በብዕር ልጽፍልህ አልወድም።
am.B: ልጽፍልህ የምችለው ብዙ ነገር አለ፤ ነገር ግን በብዕርና በቀለም ልጽፈው አልፈልግም።
am.R: የምነግርህ ብዙ ነገር አለኝ፤ ነገር ግን በደብዳቤ ልጽፈው አልፈልግም።

decisions.choice: I had many things to write: there is more I could say
decisions.reason: The imperfect εἶχον looks at the moment of writing: he had, and still has, much to say. It is near in sense to "I have".

decisions.choice: ink and pen: the tools of a letter
decisions.reason: Letters were written on papyrus with a pen cut from a reed (κάλαμος) and ink made from soot and gum (μέλαν, literally "black"). The elder prefers to speak in person. 2 John 12 closes in almost the same way.

decisions.choice: in a letter
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "ink and pen" means here.

decisions.choice: cálamo (L); pluma (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is a reed cut to a point for writing (m2). Spanish "cálamo" names exactly that, and Literal keeps it; Balanced says "pluma", the everyday word for a pen.

decisions.choice: "먹과 붓" (L, B) for ink and pen
decisions.reason: The tools of a letter (meaning decision): a reed pen and black ink. Korean "먹과 붓" are the traditional writing tools and avoid loanwords; "먹" matches 2 John 12.

source.text: ἐλπίζω δὲ εὐθέως σε ἰδεῖν, καὶ στόμα πρὸς στόμα λαλήσομεν.

records.literal_gloss: I hope but soon you to see, and mouth to mouth we will speak.

en.L: But I hope to see you soon, and we will speak mouth to mouth.
en.B: I hope instead to see you very soon, and then we can speak face to face.
en.R: I hope to come and see you soon. Then we can talk together in person.

es.L: Pero espero verte pronto, y hablaremos de viva voz.
es.B: Espero, más bien, verte muy pronto, y entonces podremos hablar en persona.

am.B: ይልቁንም በቅርቡ ላይህ ተስፋ አደርጋለሁ፤ ያን ጊዜ ፊት ለፊት እንነጋገራለን።
am.R: በቅርቡ መጥቼ ላይህ ተስፋ አደርጋለሁ። ያን ጊዜ በአካል አብረን እንነጋገራለን።

decisions.choice: mouth to mouth: in person
decisions.reason: "Mouth to mouth" is a Hebrew way of saying in person, directly (Numbers 12:8; 2 John 12).

decisions.choice: but: in place of writing more
decisions.reason: δὲ sets the hope against the unwillingness to write in verse 13: rather than write, he hopes to come.

decisions.choice: face to face (Balanced); in person (Readable)
decisions.reason: The English idiom for the same thing (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps "mouth to mouth".

decisions.choice: come and see you
decisions.reason: To see Gaius the elder must travel to him, as verse 10 says ("if I come").

decisions.choice: de viva voz (L); en persona (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 2 John 12: the idiom means speaking in person (m1), and Spanish "boca a boca" is the name of rescue breathing. Literal says "de viva voz", which keeps the picture of speech; Balanced and Readable say "en persona".

decisions.choice: de vive voix (L); face à face (B); en personne (R)
decisions.reason: As in 2 John 12: French "bouche à bouche" now means resuscitation; "de vive voix" keeps the picture of speech and means in person (m1).

decisions.choice: mdomo kwa mdomo (L); ana kwa ana (B); uso kwa uso (R)
decisions.reason: As in 2 John 12: the idiom means speaking in person (m1). Literal keeps the Greek picture; Balanced uses "ana kwa ana", the everyday Swahili for meeting in person, and Readable "uso kwa uso" (face to face).

decisions.choice: face a face
decisions.reason: As in 2 John 12: Portuguese "boca a boca" means word of mouth or resuscitation, so even Literal uses the Portuguese idiom for speaking in person (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: አፍ ለአፍ (mouth to mouth, L), ፊት ለፊት (face to face, B), as in 2 John 12
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek phrase and Balanced uses the Amharic idiom for meeting in person (meaning decision m1), as in 2 John.

fr.B: Que la paix soit avec toi.
fr.R: Que Dieu te donne la paix.

vi.B: Nguyện bình an ở cùng anh.
vi.R: Cầu xin Đức Chúa Trời ban bình an cho anh.

pt.B: Que a paz esteja com você.
pt.R: Que Deus dê paz a você.

decisions.choice: peace to you: a blessing at the close of the letter
decisions.reason: "Peace" was the Jewish greeting (shalom), and Jesus greeted his disciples with these words after he rose (John 20:19, 21, 26). As a closing blessing it asks for the well-being that comes from God (compare Ephesians 6:23; 1 Peter 5:14). The SBLGNT numbers this greeting and the two that follow as verse 15; in some Bibles, such as the King James Version, they are the end of verse 14, and 3 John has only fourteen verses.

decisions.choice: Peace be with you (Balanced); May God give you peace (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Greek has no verb. Balanced supplies the wish; Readable names God as the giver of peace (meaning decision m1).

en.B: The friends here send you greetings.

es.B: Los amigos de aquí te envían saludos.
es.R: Tus amigos de aquí te mandan saludos.

fr.B: Les amis d’ici t’envoient leurs salutations.
fr.R: Tes amis d’ici te disent bonjour.

ko.R: 이곳에 있는 당신의 친구들이 안부를 전합니다.

vi.B: Các bạn hữu ở đây gửi lời chào anh.
vi.R: Các bạn hữu của anh ở đây gửi lời chào anh.

pt.B: Os amigos daqui mandam saudações a você.
pt.R: Os seus amigos daqui mandam lembranças.

decisions.choice: the friends: fellow believers, as friends of Jesus and of one another
decisions.reason: Here φίλος stands for the believers with the elder and with Gaius. Jesus called his disciples "friends" (John 15:14-15), and Luke uses the word for Paul's fellow believers at Sidon (Acts 27:3). The word is masculine in form but covers men and women.

decisions.choice: here; send you greetings (Balanced); Your friends ... say hello (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Here" says these are the friends with the elder. "Friends" is already inclusive and needs no gender setting.

decisions.choice: "친구들" at every level, here and in the next sentence
decisions.reason: The friends are fellow believers, as friends of Jesus and of one another (meaning decision, recalling John 15:14-15); Korean keeps the word "friends", which the Korean John uses there.

decisions.choice: "các bạn hữu" for the friends (also 1:15c)
decisions.reason: The friends are fellow believers, friends of Jesus and of one another (m1); "bạn hữu" is the word the Vietnamese John uses for Jesus' friends (15:14), which keeps the echo.

decisions.choice: os amigos (no gender setting)
decisions.reason: As the English "friends": the masculine plural "amigos" is the ordinary Portuguese word for friends of both sexes, so no setting is used (meaning decision m1); the same in the next sentence.

decisions.choice: ወዳጆች (friends) at every level, as in the Amharic John 15:13-15
decisions.reason: The believers are called friends, as Jesus called his disciples friends (meaning decision m1); "ወዳጅ" is a friend who is loved, the word of the Amharic John, where "ጓደኛ" is a companion.

en.B: Greet each of the friends there by name.
en.R: Say hello to each of our friends there, one by one.

es.L: Saluda a los amigos por nombre.
es.B: Saluda a cada uno de los amigos de allá por su nombre.
es.R: Saluda a cada uno de nuestros amigos de allá, uno por uno.

fr.B: Salue chacun des amis de là-bas par son nom.
fr.R: Dis bonjour à chacun de nos amis de là-bas, un par un.

sw.B: Msalimie kila mmoja wa marafiki walioko huko kwa jina lake.
sw.R: Wasalimie marafiki zetu wote walioko huko, mmoja mmoja.

ko.B: 그곳의 친구들에게 한 사람 한 사람 이름을 불러 문안해 주십시오.
ko.R: 그곳에 있는 우리 친구들에게 한 사람씩 안부를 전해 주십시오.

vi.L: Hãy chào các bạn hữu theo từng tên.
vi.B: Xin chào từng người trong các bạn hữu ở đó.
vi.R: Xin chào từng người bạn hữu của chúng ta ở đó.

pt.B: Cumprimente cada um dos amigos daí pelo nome.
pt.R: Cumprimente cada um dos nossos amigos daí, um por um.

am.B: እዚያ ያሉትን ወዳጆች እያንዳንዳቸውን በየስማቸው ሰላም በልልኝ።
am.R: እዚያ ላሉት ወዳጆቻችን ለእያንዳንዳቸው ሰላም በልልኝ።

decisions.choice: by name: each one personally
decisions.reason: κατ ὄνομα means one by one, by their own names. The same words are used of the good shepherd, who calls his own sheep by name (John 10:3); the elder may have that in mind, but the phrase was also an ordinary one in letters.

decisions.choice: each of ... there (Balanced); each of our friends there, one by one (Readable)
decisions.reason: "There" says these are the friends with Gaius; "each" and "one by one" put "by name" (meaning decision m1) into plain words.
